segments.zh: Trees have muscles.
And they know when they are bent, even with their eyes closed.
segments.en: 而且它闭着眼，也知道自己歪了。

segments.zh: Bend one over,
and it will slowly pull itself back up.
French scientists just showed it,
segments.en: 法国科学家刚刚证明了这件事，

segments.zh: using a machine that never stops spinning.
segments.en: 用的是一台会转的机器。

segments.zh: Their paper just came out in New Phytologist.
segments.en: 论文刚登在《新植物学家》上。

segments.zh: Yes, that is a real journal name.
segments.en: 对，这本期刊真叫这个名字。

segments.zh: Start with an experiment:
lay a young poplar tree on its side.
In about ten days,
its stem curves back up toward the sky.
segments.en: 它的茎就弯着朝上长回来。

segments.zh: No surprise there.
Trees feel gravity and chase the light.
segments.en: 树能感觉重力，也追着光走。

segments.zh: Today's brain teaser:
what if there is no gravity direction and no light direction?
segments.en: 要是没有重力方向，也没有光的方向呢？

segments.zh: Does the tree still know
that it is bent?
Think about it: a tree has no eyes,
no brain, no nerves like ours.
segments.en: 也没有我们那样的大脑和神经。

segments.zh: The team built a machine:
segments.en: 研究团队造了一台机器：

segments.zh: a platform that slowly rotates.
The tree lies on it
and turns, and turns, and turns.
So gravity never points one steady way.
segments.en: 这样重力就没有固定的方向，

segments.zh: For the tree, down keeps changing.
segments.en: 从树的角度看，“下面”一直在变。

segments.zh: The whole thing sits inside a sphere
segments.en: 整个装置罩在一个球里，

segments.zh: lit equally from every side.
No up, no down,
no bright side.
Basically, a tree on a rotisserie,
segments.en: 说白了：一棵放在烤肉架上转的树，

segments.zh: inside a giant glowing ball.
segments.en: 还装在一个发光的大球里。

segments.zh: The result: over the next few weeks,
the bent stems slowly straightened out.
Almost as straight
as if nothing ever happened.
And it was not luck.
Something inside the tree was pulling.
segments.en: 树的身体里有东西在拉。

segments.zh: Twist one: the tree was not using gravity.
segments.en: 反转一：树靠的不是重力，

segments.zh: It was sensing its own shape.
That sense is called proprioception.
It is how you touch your nose with your eyes closed.
segments.en: 你闭上眼也能摸到鼻子，靠的就是它。

segments.zh: Back in 2012, the same institute showed
segments.en: 二零一二年，同一家研究所就证明了：

segments.zh: that plants have proprioception.
Robots have it too:
a sensor in every joint reports how far it is bent.
segments.en: 每个关节里有个传感器，报告自己弯了多少。

segments.zh: So how does a tree pull itself straight?
segments.en: 那树用什么把自己掰直？

segments.zh: With a special kind of wood.
segments.en: 答案是一种特别的木头。

segments.zh: It is called tension wood,
and it grows along one side of the stem.
Tension wood shrinks and pulls,
just like a muscle.
Not fast, like your muscles.
It builds up as new wood grows.
segments.en: 它是随着新木头一点点长出来的。

segments.zh: While the tree curves back up,
segments.en: 树弯着朝上长回来的时候，

segments.zh: the tension wood forms on the upper side.
Twist two, the clever one:
once the machine starts, that upper muscle stops growing.
segments.en: 机器一转，上面这块肌肉不长了。

segments.zh: And identical tension wood
starts growing on the opposite side.
It is like your arm:
biceps bend it, triceps straighten it.
segments.en: 二头肌把它弯起来，三头肌把它伸直。

segments.zh: The two pulls
slowly balance out.
And that is how the tree
pulls itself straight.
Picture a flagpole with a rope on each side:
segments.en: 想象一根旗杆，两边各拴一根绳：

segments.zh: pull both just right, and it stands tall.
segments.en: 拉得刚好，它就站得笔直。

segments.zh: The research director calls it a genuine sensorimotor loop
segments.en: 研究主任说，这是树木木头里

segments.zh: in the woody parts of trees.
segments.en: 一个真正的感觉加运动的回路。

segments.zh: Feel the bend, grow the muscle,
feel again, adjust again.
That is the same idea a robot uses
segments.en: 这跟机器人站稳的办法

segments.zh: to keep its balance.
Except a robot adjusts hundreds of times a second.
segments.en: 只不过机器人一秒钟调几百次，

segments.zh: A tree takes weeks.
Same loop.
Wildly different speed.
Twist three, the useful one:
this matters.
After storms and landslides,
trees need this trick to stand back up.
Breeding trees with a stronger sense of shape
segments.en: 挑本体感觉更强的品种，

segments.zh: might give straighter, better wood.
segments.en: 也许能长出更直、更好的木材。

segments.zh: Messy internal tension
can make the wood worse.
The researchers even hope
it could keep wheat from falling over.
Farmers call it lodging,
and it costs real harvest.
Fine print: these were young poplars in a lab.
segments.en: 友情提示：这是小杨树在实验室里的实验，

segments.zh: Big trees in the wild still need checking.
segments.en: 大树在野外怎么样，还要再看。

segments.zh: And muscle is a metaphor.
Wood is not actual muscle.
The paper says it is controlled cell by cell.
segments.en: 论文说这是一个细胞一个细胞控制的，

segments.zh: The details are still being worked out.
So, does a tree know it is bent with its eyes closed?
segments.en: 所以，树闭着眼知道自己歪了吗？

segments.zh: Yes. Then it hits the gym.
The slowest gym in the world.
One workout takes several weeks.
